summary: B closely follows the frozen contract, while A changes the established Add API’s behavior and bypasses it from Upload.
reasons: B implements the exact Upload signature, explicitly validates empty filenames and nil readers, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field "file", and delegates to FilesService.Add as required.

B leaves Add unchanged, preserving its lower-level behavior and existing error semantics. A eagerly reads and buffers every Add body, which is an out-of-scope behavioral change explicitly disallowed by the contract.
A routes Upload through a new private add method instead of the required existing Add method, duplicating the path and weakening the single-source-of-truth guarantee.

B directly tests multipart field/name/content, retry with a non-seekable io.MultiReader, validation without requests, and propagation of source-reader errors—the contract’s requested coverage areas. A omits explicit validation and source-reader-error tests for Upload.
risks_a: Changing Add to io.ReadAll introduces eager consumption, extra memory use, altered timing, and new wrapped read errors for existing callers.
Upload has no visible explicit validation before invoking the helper, despite the contract requiring it.
The original Add test is replaced and some Add-specific assertions are weakened, including method/path and full decoded filename verification.
risks_b: The retry test only inspects multipart content on the second attempt rather than asserting identical content on both attempts, though its non-seekable reader and successful retry still exercise replayability.
